# `response-header-added`

Response header added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `response-header-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Responses ([RULES.md section 6](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new response header. `Content-Type` is ignored, as OpenAPI says; names compare case-insensitively.

## Why this default

Clients ignore headers they don't know.

## Example

From test case [`response-header-added`](../../test/cases/response-header-added/): A new response header.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-           headers: {}
+           headers:
+             X-Rate-Limit:
+               schema:
+                 type: string
```

Findings:

- `response-header-added` · info · GET /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml

```
